title: How To Handle Students Who Make Classmates Laugh
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin tackles the tricky question of whether to hold an entire group accountable when one student's behavior makes classmates laugh during instructional time. He offers two keys: setting clear parameters beforehand by explicitly defining any attempt to make others laugh during instruction as a violation of the class's 'listen and follow directions' rule, and enforcing the consequence only on the instigator rather than those who merely laughed in response. He notes that repeated instances of this behavior often signal inconsistent enforcement in the past, underscoring the importance of vigilant supervision so the teacher can reliably identify who started the disruption. Applied together, he argues, these two keys eliminate the fairness dilemma and largely end the behavior.
points: Recommends explicitly defining, ahead of time, that trying to make classmates laugh during instruction breaks the class's core listening rule.
Advises enforcing consequences only on the instigator, not on students who merely laughed in response.
Notes that repeated instances of this behavior signal a need for greater consistency and vigilance from the teacher.
Frames catching the instigator in the act as essential, since inconsistent supervision undermines the whole strategy.
Positions the combination of clear pre-set parameters plus targeted enforcement as resolving the underlying fairness dilemma.
quotes: Should you hold all students who laugh accountable or just the student who started it?

Doing so is simply a matter of explaining that any behavior that attempts to make other students laugh during instructional time is a disruption and therefore transgresses rule #1 – Listen and follow directions.

The second key is to only enforce a consequence on the instigator, which attacks the misbehavior at its source and avoids the perceived unfairness of holding accountable those who, sometimes against their will, laughed.
It’s important to mention that when students repeatedly try to make others laugh, it’s a sign that you’ve been less than consistent in the past.
If your back is turned and you don’t know who misbehaved, then you’re out of luck.
With these two keys, plus your vigilance, this and other similar disruptions will rarely if ever happen again.
